title: Field need lattice and release proposals — compact brief
body:
Objective and scope:
This working brief bundles recent field signals into a compact lattice of customer needs, proposed release patches, and lightweight probes. The goal is to recommend 3 near-term fixes (<=2 sprints), 2 medium-term product changes (1–3 quarters), and measurable experiments to validate cost/latency tradeoffs.

How this doc is organized (quick nav):
- TL;DR summary
- Top 8 customer asks (clustered by theme) with impact hypothesis
- Quick patches (1–2 sprint, low risk) + owners
- Medium bets and product proposals (design notes + gating risks)
- Experiment plan (metrics, instrumentation)
- Customer quotes and evidence
- Open questions / engineering constraints
- Concrete next steps and owners

TL;DR summary:
Customers consistently ask for clearer cost signals (per-call breakout), safer rollout controls (per-customer canary + pause), and small runtime knobs to avoid tail-latency spikes. Several enterprise accounts are delaying Dedicated onboarding citing uncertainty around burst billing and cache warmup behavior.

Top 8 clustered asks (short):
1) Per-request cost attribution visible in Console and billing exports (high impact — reduces finance churn)
   - Impact hypothesis: showing token-level + batching attribution will shorten procurement cycles for 3–5 mid-market customers.
2) Pauseable canary and instant rollback at customer/model granularity (high reliability need)
   - Reason: ops teams want to pause rollout mid-canary when quality regressions show up in eval probes.
3) KV cache visibility and TTL controls (medium impact)
   - Customers want to understand prefix hit rates and set per-app TTLs to reduce cold-start token charges.
4) Predictable burst billing cap or soft-limits for Dedicated (high commercial friction)
   - Enterprise customers fear unexpected overages during peak events.
5) Model variant tagging and auto-fallback policies surfaced in API responses (medium)
   - When fallback happens due to capacity, apps need to know which variant served the response.
6) Better default batching heuristics tuned for short-turn prompts (low latency apps) (medium)
7) Console route-level SLO summaries and alerts (low/medium)
8) Embeddings indexing preview + sample-cost estimator (medium)

Quick patches (<=2 sprints) — proposed: 
- Patch A: Add per-request billing metadata header (X-RW-COST-ESTIMATE) in the response with conservative token + batch attribution. Owner: Diego Ramos (cs->eng routing). Effort: ~3 dev days + 1 day docs. Risk: low.
- Patch B: Console toggle — show last 7-day KV cache hit-rate per model route. Owner: Katherine (product). Effort: ~1 sprint. Risk: medium (needs runtime metrics export).
- Patch C: Canary pause API (POST /rollouts/{id}/pause). Owner: Morgan Li -> SRE/rollouts eng. Effort: ~5 days. Risk: medium (race conditions).

Medium-term product proposals (1–3 quarters):
- Proposal 1: Burst soft-cap for Dedicated with queued overflow and opt-in charged buffer. Description: add a configurable soft cap per-reservation that throttles non-critical requests while allowing critical routes to burst. Includes billing preview sim. Dependencies: scheduler + billing. Risks: complexity in fairness.
- Proposal 2: Per-tenant cache control API + inference preview. Allow customers to declare predictable prefix patterns and TTL guesses; runtime will expose warmup predictions and estimated token-savings pre-deploy. Benefits: lowers perceived unpredictability of on-demand costs. Gating: instrumentation + UI work.

Experiment plan (how we validate, KPIs):
Goal: reduce finance objections and shorten Dedicated contracts by 20% (time-to-close) for target cohort.
Experiments: 
- E1: Roll per-request billing header to 10 pilot customers for 6 weeks. Measure: change in negotiation time, number of billing follow-ups, support tickets.
- E2: Expose route-level cache hit rates + TTL control to 5 customers and see change to average tokens/response over 4 weeks. Measure: median tokens per request, adoption of TTL settings.
- E3: Canary pause in 8 teams — track time-to-fix and rollback frequency. Measure: incidents avoided and mean time to remediation.
Instrumentation needs: event emitted for fallback (variant id), cache hit/miss per request, rollout pause/resume events, per-request cost estimate calculation.

Customer quotes and evidence (verbatim / anonymized):
- "We can't justify moving to Dedicated if one traffic spike can blow our committed budget. We need a way to cap burst or at least preview the worst-case cost." — Large fintech, EU sales cycle.
- "When we saw a sudden 300ms tail on certain routes, it took ages to trace — some visibility into the cache/kv behavior would have saved us hours." — Mid-market ISV.
- "Having a single metric that says 'this response used variant X (q4)' would let our feature flags react." — Platform engineering lead at a consumer app.

Open questions and constraints from engineering conversations:
- How precise can the per-request cost estimate be without a full tokenization pass in the front-plane? We need approximation rules and guardrails to avoid overpromising.
- KV cache telemetry: runtime currently aggregates on worker-local metrics; exporting per-route hit-rate at request granularity will add cardinality and cost. Need sampling strategy.
- Canary pause semantics: do we block in-flight requests or only prevent new allocations? Design must avoid deadlocks in the autoscaler.

Risk map (concise):
- Billing headers: low user-facing risk but legal/compliance review required for showing estimated charges.
- Cache control API: moderate engineering risk (complexity + storage of TTL configs).
- Burst soft-cap: high product & sales impact if poorly implemented (can block traffic unexpectedly).

Recommended next steps (concrete owners + timelines):
1) Ship Patch A (billing header) to pilots — Diego — target: deploy alpha by 2026-07-21.
2) Start instrumentation spike for KV metrics sampling — Katherine + Infra team — 2-week spike starting 2026-07-08.
3) Draft policy doc for Dedicated burst soft-cap (product + finance) — Morgan — due 2026-07-15.
4) Align with Legal on billing disclosures for header and console preview — Aisha — 1 week.

Operational notes / playbook additions (quick):
- Add a CS checklist for customers being onboarded to Dedicated: review burst policy, show billing header, enable KV preview if applicable.
- Create a short KB article for "Why my tokens spiked" explaining cache warmup, batching, and variant fallback.

Appendix: quick measurement definitions
- Time-to-close (procurement): days between final demo and signed contract.
- Tokens per response: the measured token consumption including system/prefix tokens.
- Cache hit-rate (route): sampled ratio of hits / (hits + misses) over 1 hour window.

Notes to self / fragments: 
- Possible quick UI: in routes list, small badge "cache: 62% (7d)" with a tooltip linking to example requests.
- Investigate adding a low-overhead hashed-prefix sampler at ingress to estimate warm prefixes without full tracing.
- Consider an "emergency-throttle" API that CS can toggle for a customer when finance/overage disputes arise.

Concluding thought:
This lattice synthesizes a lot of existing voices into implementable pieces. The shortest path to reduced friction seems to be better cost-signal visibility (header + console) + the ability to stop a rollout quickly. If we can show measurable wins in pilot accounts within 6 weeks we should see a meaningful improvement in Dedicated conversion friction.

Document history and provenance:
- Compiled from: 9 field interviews (May–Jun 2026), support ticket crawl (120 tickets flagged as "billing" or "latency"), and 2 product-ops syncs.
- Owner for follow-up: Morgan Li (morgan.li@redwood.com)

End of brief.
